error: The request could not be completed
supportBoundary: Network controls remain unverified until the configured topology passes lab isolation tests.
helpIntro: Practical guidance for every Suro workflow.
ownerSeparation: User-reported identity and the permanent device owner are distinct. Only an administrator assigns or verifies the owner. Military rank is optional.
searchOwner: Search device, owner, or Windows user…
templateStaged: Saving a template does not apply it. Preview compatibility and approve the resulting batch separately.
apRegistrationNotice: Use a dedicated management account and verified TLS. Discovery preserves existing configuration. Legacy routers can use API-SSL with a trusted certificate.
archiveNotice: Archiving removes the device from monitoring. Its router configuration and historical records are retained.
batchSafetyNotice: Review every target and backup. One AP runs at a time by default. A failed target stops the batch. Reboots and radio changes interrupt users; preserve another management path.
confirmTargets: I approve these exact targets and changes
protectedNames: Type protected device names, separated by commas
outOfBandConfirmed: A tested out-of-band recovery path is available
network.read_only: Read-only observation or backup; no configuration replacement.
WAITING_RECONNECT: Waiting for return and uptime verification
inferenceNotice: Observed facts and probable causes are shown separately. Confidence is an estimate; review evidence before remediation.
topologyNotice: Logical relationships only. Solid links have recent observations; dashed links are unknown. No physical uplink is invented from a shared subnet.
recoveryNotice: Automatic recovery is off by default. It needs persistent corroborated evidence, a reachable API, maintenance approval, alternate management paths, cooldowns and attempt limits. Gateways and protected infrastructure are excluded.

credential.PENDING_APPLY: Generated, not yet set on the computer
revealNotice: The password is shown once, and the request is recorded in the audit log with your reason. Requires a recent two-factor sign-in. Do not copy it into chats or files.
closeAfterUse: Close this window as soon as you have used the password.
randomPasswordNotice: For new computers. Suro creates a strong random password and stores it encrypted. Nothing changes on the computer: set this password on the administrator account during setup, then record the result. Replacing an existing record does not change the password on the computer.
legacyMacNotice: Computers set up with the old kursant script have an AcademyAdmin password calculated from their Wi-Fi MAC address. Choose the address the adapter had when the script ran. Nothing changes on the computer. If sign-in fails, try the next address.
recordCredentialNotice: After signing in to the computer with this password, record whether it worked. A failed result marks the computer for manual recovery; Suro never resets passwords.
credentialOwnerOnly: Only an administrator with the owner role can view or change local administrator passwords.
legacyAllowedAddresses: Addresses allowed by the old firewall
legacyStandardUser: Standard user named by the old script
legacyNotReported: This agent has not reported old-script information yet. Update the agent and run a recheck.
legacy.admin_account_present: The AcademyAdmin account from the old script exists. Keep it until another administrator account is confirmed working.
legacy.firewall_reset_at_boot: An old startup task resets Windows Firewall at every boot and re-applies its own outbound allowlist. Suro firewall rules are removed on each restart until this task is retired.
legacy.server_blocked_after_boot: The Suro server address is not in the old allowlist: after a restart this computer cannot reach Suro.
legacy.server_address_unverified: Suro's address is a host name, so it cannot be compared with the old allowlist. Check that the server IP is listed.
legacy.winre_disabled: Windows Recovery Environment was disabled by the old script. Re-enable it before any disk or partition work.
credential.exists: A credential is already recorded for this computer.
credential.not_found: No administrator credential is recorded for this computer.
credential.concurrent_change: Someone else changed this record. Reload and try again.
explorerIntro: Access point groups, access points and the computers on them. Each status shows only what its own source proves: being registered does not mean a computer is on, and a computer missing from Wi-Fi lists may simply be wired.
bucket.agent_only: Agent reporting, not seen on Wi-Fi
selectNodeHint: Select an access point or computer to see its details.
searchExplorer: Search by name, owner or MAC
sourceNote.registered: Registered: the computer is in the Suro device registry. That alone says nothing about whether it is switched on.
sourceNote.wifi: Wi-Fi: the newest association list from polled MikroTik access points, trusted for 3 minutes. Wired computers and access points Suro does not poll never appear there, so their Wi-Fi status is unknown rather than offline.
sourceNote.agent: Agent: signed heartbeats from the Suro Windows service. Silent means no heartbeat within the configured deadline.
sourceNote.compliance: Compliance: the latest verified agent evidence checked against the assigned policy. Missing or old evidence is shown as unverified, never as compliant.
legacyTaskActive: active – resets the firewall at every boot
retireLegacyTaskNotice: The task is disabled, not deleted, and a copy is saved on the computer. The firewall rules in effect now stay as they are, so the connection to Suro does not change; they just stop being reset at boot. Runs only in Maintenance or Approved remediation mode.
restoreLegacyTaskNotice: Turns the old task back on. From the next boot it again resets Windows Firewall and removes Suro's firewall rules.
replaceLegacyRulesNotice: Applies the policy's firewall allowlist and disables (does not delete) the three old "Allow outbound to …" rules. A full firewall backup is taken first. If HTTPS to the Suro server cannot be confirmed, the backup is restored automatically. The policy must explicitly allow the Suro server address and port.
maintenance.legacy_task_active: The old kursant startup task is still active and would remove these firewall rules at the next boot. Disable it first.
maintenance.legacy_state_unknown: This agent has not reported the old-script state yet. Update the agent and run a recheck first.
maintenance.legacy_task_not_reported: The agent has not reported the old startup task on this computer.
policyCategory.accounts.hint: Which Windows accounts each computer must have, and who may be an administrator.
policyCategory.disk.hint: Where Windows and user files live. Suro checks the layout but never repartitions a disk on its own.
policyCategory.network.hint: How each computer gets its network address.
policyCategory.firewall.hint: Keeps computers off the public internet while Suro and approved local services stay reachable.
policyCategory.system.hint: Small Windows adjustments for the standard user.
policyCategory.software.hint: Whether administrators may install software from Suro on these computers.
policyCategory.agent.hint: How often the Suro client reports and how long its results stay valid.
policyCategory.advanced.hint: Compliance rules and automatic network isolation. Change these only if you understand the effects.
policySetting.require_admin_account.help: Each computer must have the administrator account named below, enabled and in the Administrators group. Suro checks this; it does not create the account.
policySetting.admin_account.help: The local Windows account administrators use. Up to 20 letters, digits, - or _, starting with a letter.
policySetting.require_standard_user.help: Each computer must have the everyday user account named below, and it must not be an administrator.
policySetting.user_account.help: The account people use every day. Same naming rules as the administrator account.
policySetting.demote_standard_user: Automatically remove administrator rights from the standard user
policySetting.demote_standard_user.help: If the standard user is in the Administrators group, the Suro client removes it, but only when a working administrator account exists. Only in Continuous or Approved remediation mode. Files are not touched.
policySetting.approved_admins: Other accounts allowed to be administrators
policySetting.approved_admins.help: Administrator accounts that are expected. Any other administrator is reported, never removed.
policySetting.legacy_admin_accepted.help: Computers prepared with the old kursant script have an AcademyAdmin administrator. Turn this on so it is not reported as unexpected. Its password is on the computer's Local administrator tab.
policySetting.preserve_user_files.help: No policy setting deletes, moves or overwrites user files. This cannot be switched off.
policySetting.require_d: Require separate C: and D: partitions
policySetting.require_d.help: Each computer must have a healthy NTFS D: volume. Suro reports computers without one; creating it is a manual job done after a backup.
policySetting.min_d_gb.help: A smaller D: volume is reported. 0 means any size.
policySetting.require_user_data_on_d.hel: The standard user's Documents, Desktop, Pictures, Videos and Downloads must point to D:. Suro reports this; folders are moved by hand after a backup.
policySetting.backup_before_disk_changes: Back up before any disk change
Disk work always needs a verified backup and its own approval first.
policySetting.no_automatic_repartition.h: Suro never shrinks, formats or creates partitions because of a policy. A computer without D: is marked for manual work.
policySetting.protect_system_files: Extra protection for system files on C:
policySetting.protect_system_files.help: Not available yet. Windows' own permissions already stop standard users from changing system files; Suro adds and checks nothing more.
policySetting.ip_mode.help: How the computer should get its address. Suro checks the network adapter used for the default route and reports differences. It does not change network settings yet.
policySetting.ip_prefix.help: The network the computers' addresses belong to, for example 192.168.10.0/24.
policySetting.ip_gateway.help: The router's address in that network, for example 192.168.10.1.
policySetting.dns_servers.help: Up to four local DNS server addresses, in order of use.
policySetting.static_address_per_compute: Each computer's own address is set on the Assign tab. Suro refuses an address another computer or DHCP reservation already uses.
policySetting.verify_connectivity: Check the connection to Suro after network changes
policySetting.verify_connectivity.help: Any approved network or firewall change is undone automatically if the computer can no longer reach Suro.
policySetting.apply_ip_configuration.hel: Not available yet. Suro only reports whether the computer matches; change the address by hand or with a DHCP reservation.
policySetting.block_internet.help: Prevents this computer from connecting to the public internet. Communication with the Suro server and the local services below stays allowed. The firewall changes only through an approved maintenance job that checks the connection and rolls back on failure.
The Suro server's address and port always stay allowed, so blocking the internet never cuts off management.
policySetting.firewall_allowances.help: Local addresses the computer may still reach, such as a file server or printer. Public internet addresses are refused.
policySetting.firewall_auto_enable: Turn Windows Firewall back on automatically
policySetting.firewall_auto_enable.help: If someone switches Windows Firewall off, the Suro client turns it back on (Continuous or Approved remediation mode).
policySetting.hide_c: Hide drive C: in File Explorer
policySetting.hide_c.help: Hides C: in the standard user's File Explorer. A convenience, not a security barrier: programs can still open C:. Takes effect after the user signs in again.
policySetting.hide_c_auto.help: Lets the Suro client set this for the standard user while they are signed in (Continuous or Approved remediation mode).
When off, Suro refuses to send software, drivers or language packs to these computers. Suro client updates are still allowed.
policySetting.heartbeat_seconds.help: Time between status reports and policy checks. Shorter is fresher but adds load on the server. Older clients keep the interval they were installed with.
policySetting.heartbeat_deadline_seconds: Treat a computer as offline after
With no report in this time, Suro shows the computer as offline and stops trusting its last results.
policySetting.evidence_ttl_seconds.help: Older results count as unverified, never as compliant.
policySetting.offline_policy_cache: Keep working while the server is unreachable
policySetting.offline_policy_cache.help: The client keeps the last signed policy for up to 24 hours and keeps checking.
policySetting.automatic_retry.help: Not available yet. Interrupted work is reported as unknown and never repeated automatically, so a risky change is not repeated.
policySetting.mandatory_checks.help: A computer is compliant only when every selected requirement is confirmed. Core security checks are always included.
policySetting.quarantine_on_failure: Isolate noncompliant computers from the network
policySetting.quarantine_on_failure.help: Asks the router to restrict computers that stay noncompliant after the waiting time. The computer may lose network access.
policySetting.quarantine_on_missing_hear: Restricts computers whose Suro client stops reporting. This can cut off a computer that was only switched off.
How long a computer may stay noncompliant before isolation starts.
enforcement.agent.help: The Suro client changes this itself, in Continuous or Approved remediation mode.
enforcement.approval.help: Changed only by a separately approved maintenance job that checks the connection and rolls back.
enforcement.detected.help: The client checks and reports this. Nothing on the computer is changed.
enforcement.server.help: The Suro server acts on this setting; nothing changes on the computer.
enforcement.protected.help: A safety rule that cannot be switched off.
enforcement.unavailable.help: Suro does not do this yet and never reports it as met.
risk.safe.title: Safe changes
risk.safe.explain: Checked or applied without interrupting users.
risk.restart.title: Changes that need a sign-in or restart
risk.restart.explain: They take effect after the user signs in again or the computer restarts.
risk.network.title: Changes that can affect network communication
risk.network.explain: Firewall and address changes run only as approved jobs that check the connection to Suro and undo the change if it fails.
risk.high.title: High-risk requirements
risk.high.explain: Disk and account requirements are only checked. Computers that miss them are reported for planned, backed-up manual work; nothing is repartitioned or removed automatically.
autoOp.account.demote_user: Remove admin rights from the standard user
check.account.admin.exists.fix: Create the administrator account during setup, then recheck.
check.account.admin.member_of_administra: Add the administrator account to the Administrators group.
check.account.user.exists.fix: Create the standard user account, then recheck.
check.account.user.not_administrator: Standard user is not an administrator
check.account.user.not_administrator.fix: Remove the user from Administrators, or turn on automatic removal and use Approved remediation mode.
Review the listed accounts: add expected ones to the allowed administrators, or remove their rights by hand.
check.disk.c.valid.fix: Run a disk check during maintenance.
check.disk.d.valid: D: partition is present and large enough
check.disk.d.valid.fix: Plan manual partitioning after a verified backup; see the computer's Storage tab.
check.disk.user_data_location.valid.fix: Move the user's folders to D: in planned maintenance, after a backup.
check.firewall.enabled.fix: Turn the firewall on, or enable automatic correction.
check.firewall.outbound_policy.valid.fix: Run the approved firewall job from the computer's page in Maintenance mode.
check.firewall.managed_rules.valid: Only approved firewall rules allow traffic
check.firewall.managed_rules.valid.fix: Review other allow rules and migrate them through the approved firewall job.
check.network.ip_reservation.valid.fix: Create or check the DHCP reservation under Network infrastructure.
check.network.mac_identity.valid.fix: Check that the computer's MAC address is registered on the access point.
check.network.internet_restriction.valid: Suro cannot yet verify router-side restriction; check the MikroTik firewall.
check.network.isolation.valid.fix: Suro cannot yet verify router-side isolation.
check.security.user_restrictions.valid.f: Suro cannot verify this yet; untick it in Advanced settings if it blocks compliance.
check.agent.service_running.fix: Start the Suro service or reinstall the client.
check.agent.integrity_valid: Suro client is genuine and unmodified
check.agent.policy_version_current: Computer uses the current policy version
check.agent.policy_version_current.fix: Wait for the computer to check in, or run a recheck.
check.endpoint.ip_configuration.valid.fi: Change the address by hand or with a DHCP reservation, then recheck. Clients older than 0.2 cannot report this.
policy.invalid: Some settings are invalid. Fix the highlighted items.
policy.invalid_prefix: Enter a private network such as 192.168.10.0/24 (prefix 8–30).
policy.static_prefix_required: Fixed addresses need a network and prefix.
policy.invalid_gateway: The gateway is not a valid address.
policy.gateway_outside_prefix: The gateway must be inside the network, and not its first or last address.
policy.invalid_dns: A DNS server address is not valid.
policy.invalid_static_address: The computer's address is not valid.
policy.static_address_outside_prefix: The computer's address must be inside the policy's network.
policy.static_address_is_gateway: The computer's address cannot be the gateway.
policy.static_fields_without_static_mode: Network, gateway and DNS are used only with fixed (static) addresses.
policy.min_d_without_d: A minimum D: size needs the D: partition requirement.
policy.invalid_account_name: Account names start with a letter and use only letters, digits, - and _ (up to 20).
policy.out_of_range: The value is outside the allowed range.
policy.unknown_setting: The document contains a setting Suro does not know.
policy.management_not_allowed: Blocking the internet would also block the Suro server. Add the Suro server rule.
policy.management_address_unverified: Suro's address is a host name, so Suro cannot check that the firewall keeps it reachable. Make sure its IP address is allowed.
policy.dns_blocked: This DNS server is not among the allowed services, so name lookups would be blocked:
policy.deployment_disabled: Software, driver and language-pack installation will be refused for these computers.
policy.disk_changes_manual: Computers without a D: partition will be reported for manual, backed-up work; nothing is repartitioned automatically.
policy.draft_changed: Someone else saved this draft. Reload to see their changes.
policy.draft_is_only_copy: This draft has never been published, so it cannot be discarded.
policy.nothing_to_publish: There are no draft changes to publish.
policy.not_published: Publish the policy before assigning it.
policy.no_targets: Choose at least one computer or group.
policy.duplicate_static_address: This address is already used by another computer.
policy.static_address_device_only: A fixed address can be set only for a single computer.
deployment.disabled_by_policy: The policy of at least one selected computer does not allow software installation.
ps.intro: Create and publish settings for Windows computers without editing code. Changes reach computers only after you publish and assign them.
ps.noPoliciesHint: Create one from a template to get started.
ps.template.standard.hint: Managed administrator and user, user data on D:, internet blocked, reserved addresses, firewall kept on.
ps.template.restricted.hint: Like Standard, plus automatic removal of admin rights from the user and drive C: hidden.
ps.template.maintenance.hint: For technicians' work: reports more often and makes no automatic changes.
ps.template.custom.hint: Suro's safe defaults; adjust everything yourself.
ps.discardConfirm: Discard the draft and return to the published version?
ps.draftSaved: Draft saved. Computers are not affected until you publish.
ps.unsavedConfirm: You have unsaved changes. Leave without saving?
ps.saveAsTemplate: Mark the copy as a template
ps.notAppliedAutomatically: Checked, or applied only after separate approval
ps.noChanges: No changes compared with the published version.
ps.affects: You are changing the policy for {n} computers.
ps.firstVersion: This is the first version of this policy. It affects no computers until you assign it.
ps.noComputersYet: No computers use this policy yet.
ps.onlineOffline: {online} online computers receive it within minutes; {offline} offline computers receive it when they reconnect.
ps.desiredNotForced: Publishing sets the desired configuration. Disk, account and network changes are never forced: they are checked, and risky work needs its own approval.
ps.understandRisk: I understand which changes may affect users or network access.
ps.publishBeforeAssign: Publish this policy before assigning it to computers.
ps.precedence: Each computer uses one policy. Inside it, later layers win: the policy itself, then overrides for all computers, a computer type, a computer group and a single computer. Overrides that weaken security need separate approval, and two groups that disagree must be resolved for each computer.
ps.allComputersHint: Computers added later need a new assignment. Developer devices are never included.
ps.groupsNotAp: Windows computer groups. Access point groups are separate and never receive Windows policy.
ps.assignOnline: {n} are online and receive it within minutes.
ps.assignOffline: {n} are offline and receive it when they reconnect.
ps.assignConfirm: Assign the published policy to {n} computers? Their compliance shows as unverified until they report again.
ps.staticAddressesHint: Give each computer its own address inside {prefix}. It applies after the policy is published again.
ps.staticAfterPublish: The address is checked for duplicates now and applies to the computer after the next publication.
ps.complianceTruth: These numbers come from what computers reported, not from what was sent. A computer counts as compliant only after it has confirmed every requirement.
ps.noReportYet: This computer has not reported results for this version yet.
ps.restoreHint: Copies this version into the draft. Nothing reaches computers until you review and publish it.
ps.advancedHint: For technical staff: the policy exactly as stored. Edits are checked by the same server rules as the visual editor and only change the draft.
ps.advancedApplied: Applied to the draft. Save the draft to keep it.
policy.layer_incompatible: A computer-specific override no longer fits this version. Remove or change it first.
